To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Brian’s Monday brief: Embakasi casuals’ pay and Kisumu loading, 30 November

DRAFT — for Achieng’s review before use

Brian,

Thank you for taking this on. Six years working together and I know you won’t need a speech from me, but you do need the facts and somewhere to draw the line on promises. Here’s what we know tonight and how I suggest we handle Monday.

The main thing: this is our mess, not theirs. The guys did nothing wrong. Go in with an apology, not a defence of management.

WHAT HAPPENED TO FRIDAY’S PAY

The bank rejected the entire casuals’ payment file at 1:52pm on Friday. It covered 212 people. Following the bank’s platform upgrade on 25 November, the beneficiary-reference field in our file was too long for the new template. No payments in that file were processed. This wasn’t a case of some payments going through slowly.

The rejection alert went to the old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, by which time the bank cut-off had passed. We failed both to get the file through and to catch the rejection in time.

Kevin proposed switching the payments to M-Pesa bulk. Njeri approved that on Saturday morning. She also approved KES 500 for lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list, to be paid in the same M-Pesa batch. The company covers the M-Pesa charges; they are not to be deducted from anyone’s pay.

Kevin’s latest estimate is Monday by 11am. That is the working expectation, not a guaranteed receipt time. Approval to proceed is not confirmation that the batch has been sent or that every phone has received money.

Peninah has confirmed 198 numbers. She could not reach the remaining 14, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. “Unreachable” does not mean those numbers are necessarily wrong, and it certainly does not mean those people lose their pay. She will be at Embakasi from 7:30am with the printout to check them face to face. She is also bringing her laptop for anyone who wants a printed payslip.

BEFORE THE GROUP GATHERS

You’re getting there at 5:30. Please speak to Joseph first: get the overnight picture, check who is there and establish where you can talk without everyone having to shout across the loading area.

Then speak to Ouma privately, before addressing the whole group. Joseph says he and two others are encouraging people not to load until they see the money. Take that seriously without treating him as the enemy. He has four children and rent to think about. Being loud doesn’t make his concern unreasonable.

Something along these lines is enough:

“Ouma, I wanted to talk to you first. Friday’s pay failed on our side, and I’m sorry. I know people have bills waiting. I’ll explain what is approved and what is still being checked, but I’m not going to give you a time I can’t stand behind. Tell me what people are most worried about, then let’s talk to everyone properly.”

Listen before asking for cooperation. Don’t ask him to guarantee the others will work or make him responsible for everybody’s behaviour.

I’m awake from 4:30am. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes: payment status, the mood at the depot, or a refusal to load. My flight leaves at 7:05, so don’t assume I’ll be reachable right up to 7.

WHAT TO SAY TO EVERYONE

“Morning, everyone. I owe you an apology on behalf of management. You worked, your pay was due on Friday, and we did not get it to you. You did nothing wrong.

“The bank rejected our payment file because it did not meet the updated format requirements. We also missed the rejection alert until after the bank cut-off. None of the payments in that file went through.

“Payment through M-Pesa has now been approved. Finance’s current expectation is Monday by 11am, but I cannot guarantee that every phone will have received money by then, and I won’t pretend otherwise.

“Every person on the affected list will also receive KES 500 for Monday lunch and fare in the same payment batch. The company is covering the M-Pesa charges.

“Peninah will be here at 7:30 with the list. There are 14 people she hasn’t been able to reach, so she needs to check their numbers directly. Please speak to her privately about your number or any pay query. She can also help with printed payslips.

“I know another promise is not the same as money received. I will keep you updated, including if there is a delay. The Kisumu trucks need to leave at 9, and I am asking you to help us get them loaded while we sort out the payments. I understand that means asking you to work before the expected payment time.”

Then take questions. Don’t argue with someone describing what the delay has cost them.

PROMISES AND LIMITS

You can confirm the approved payment route, the KES 500 for every affected casual and company-paid M-Pesa charges. None of those is conditional on agreeing to load.

You can promise a clear next update and your own availability. At the first briefing, tell them you will update them at 8am, even if all you have is an honest “not yet confirmed”. Give another update before the 9am departure deadline, and sooner if the facts change.

You cannot promise payment before loading, before the trucks leave, or at an exact hour. Do not turn Kevin’s “realistic by 11” into “everyone will definitely have it at 11”. We learnt that in Mombasa in 2024: “by lunch” became 4pm, and half the shift sat down. Never again a time we cannot keep.

Do not promise the 14 outstanding checks will all be resolved immediately at 7:30. Ask Kevin and Peninah to confirm how corrected numbers will be handled, and whether any individual payment will fall outside the expected timing. Give those people a specific follow-up rather than letting them disappear into the general update.

If someone asks for compensation beyond the approved KES 500, hear them out and record it for HR. Don’t approve an extra amount on the spot.

THE 9AM KISUMU DEADLINE

The trucks need to leave by 9 to make the mill’s offloading slot. Our current payment expectation is two hours later. We must not build Monday’s plan around money arriving before departure.

Before the shift starts, have Joseph check the loading requirement with you and work backwards from 9am to the latest workable loading start. Agree when a delay needs to be escalated to whoever coordinates dispatch and the mill. Do not wait until 9 to announce that the slot is at risk.

Ask for cooperation honestly. Don’t offer priority payment to people who load, threaten to withhold the KES 500 from those who don’t, or use the truck deadline to pressure Kevin into an earlier promise.

IF OUMA’S GROUP REFUSES TO LOAD

Stay calm and find out exactly what they are saying: who is refusing, what work is affected and what they want addressed. Keep the loading area safe. Don’t argue around moving trucks or try to force a confrontation.

Speak with Ouma and the others away from the wider crowd if they are willing. Repeat what is confirmed, acknowledge that payment is overdue and ask whether they will resume loading while the payment process continues. Don’t describe silence or a vague response as an agreement.

The procedure requires any stoppage to be handled jointly by Operations and HR. You are the Operations lead; you are not being asked to make the HR decisions alone. Contact me immediately if a stoppage starts or looks imminent. Before I board, we need a named HR contact for the period I’m in the air. Peninah’s payroll presence does not automatically make her the HR decision-maker. If cover is not confirmed, escalate that gap rather than assuming you have authority to handle the stoppage alone.

No dismissal, threats of dismissal or threats about contracts on Monday. That is in the procedure, and it applies even if the trucks miss the slot.

Keep a factual note of the times, concerns raised, work affected, what was said and who was contacted. No labels like “troublemakers”. The normal grievance route is through the shift supervisor, then HR within 48 hours; explain that route without using it to shut down Monday’s conversation.

If loading will not finish in time, escalate the transport consequences early and arrange the operational response through dispatch. A missed slot is a problem to manage, not a reason to abandon the joint procedure.

PAYMENT FOLLOW-THROUGH

Get Kevin’s latest status before the first briefing if possible. Ask what is actually confirmed, what remains outstanding and whether the 11am expectation still holds.

Once payments start, check for exceptions with Peninah rather than assuming a batch submission means everyone has been paid. If 11am passes with anyone unpaid, acknowledge it directly, get an individual status and give the next update time. No rolling “another hour” promises without evidence.

Thanks, Brian. Be straight with them, give them room to be angry, and don’t leave anyone guessing. I’ll review this tonight and we’ll settle the HR cover before I fly.

Achieng
